business: Remi, an Arabic/English kitchen app (pantry tracking, receipt scanning, meal planning, shopping list) with an optional countertop device
target: Arabic-speaking adults, 25 to 45, who run the kitchen and grocery shopping for a household of 3+ in the Gulf or North Africa
where: MENA: Gulf (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar) and North Africa (Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia); online, app stores

segments.name: North Africa young couple / student-age household

behaviours.name: Weekly big shop
behaviours.how: Does one large hypermarket shop a week (Carrefour, Lulu, Hyper One) and keeps a mental list.

behaviours.name: Delivery-app regular
behaviours.how: Orders groceries on Talabat, Noon or Breadfast several times a week, rarely plans ahead.

behaviours.name: Recipe-video cook
behaviours.how: Picks dinners from Instagram, TikTok or YouTube cooking videos on the day.

behaviours.name: Health and diet tracker
behaviours.how: Counts calories or protein, has tried MyFitnessPal or a diet plan.

behaviours.name: Budget-conscious
behaviours.how: Watches every price, hates subscriptions, compares offers.

behaviours.name: Family WhatsApp list
behaviours.how: The household shares the shopping list in a WhatsApp group; a helper or spouse does some of the shopping.

behaviours.name: Gadget early adopter
behaviours.how: Owns smart-home devices, buys new tech early, reads reviews.

objections: I won't keep logging every item I buy and use
Another subscription? Most of these apps are free
My mother / my helper manages the kitchen, not an app
WhatsApp and my memory already work fine
Receipt scanning never reads Arabic receipts properly
Why would I need a separate device on the counter when I have my phone?
I don't trust an app with my family's data
Recipes in these apps are Western, not what we cook
habits: you cook dinner for the family most nights
you throw away vegetables at least once a week because they went off
Ramadan changes how your household shops and cooks for a month
you already pay for one or two app subscriptions (streaming, music)
a domestic helper does part of the cooking
you split shopping with your spouse and often buy duplicates
